profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap point is labeled "Google - Thornton" and sits on Grant Street in Thornton, Colorado, in the Denver metro area, but Google's own data center locations page does not list a Colorado facility among its named hyperscale campuses, and this registry could not independently confirm Google as the current tenant or owner of any Thornton building through a tier-1 Google source this session. Several third-party data center aggregators, including Baxtel and a data center tracker site, independently refer to a "West Tower" Google-associated facility in Thornton, and job listing sites have posted Google Data Center Technician roles for Thornton, Colorado, which together suggest some kind of operational Google presence in the area, whether a leased colocation suite, an edge facility, or a smaller operation not included on Google's public campus list. A Marcus & Millichap commercial real estate listing for a "Grant Street Data Center" in Thornton describes a 267,177-square-foot data center and office facility on 12.07 acres, marketed for sale at $28 million with existing carrier connectivity from Comcast, Verizon, CenturyLink, AT&T, and Dish; that listing does not name Google as a tenant, owner, or user, so this registry cannot treat the building's size as a confirmed Google fact, only as an independently sourced description of a data center building at this Thornton address. Given the absence of any operator-confirmed source tying Google directly to a specific Thornton building, this registry declines to assign Google-specific address, square footage, or capacity figures to this point beyond what OpenStreetMap itself records, rather than adopting aggregator or job-listing evidence as proof of a hyperscale Google facility.

Google's broader data center disclosure practice, as seen across other facilities in this registry, is to name specific campuses on its own datacenters.google site while withholding building-level addresses, capacity, and square footage even for confirmed sites; the total absence of Thornton from that list, combined with a real estate listing that never names Google, makes this Colorado record a genuinely weaker case than a confirmed-but-undisclosed Google building elsewhere, not merely an unusually quiet one.

reading.body:
This facility's capacity is not published. Third-party aggregators list a Google presence at this Thornton address under the name West Tower, and job postings corroborate operational staff, but the facility does not appear on Google's official datacenters list, suggesting it may be a smaller leased or edge installation rather than one of Google's named hyperscale campuses. Research status is exhausted.

Colorado has 17 mapped data center facilities, of which only 3 publish power specifications totaling 26.35 MW. This facility's published capacity rank within the state cannot be determined because no figure is available for it. The state context therefore does not constrain interpretation of its scale.

Without published specifications, this facility cannot be read as a binding constraint on AI scaling or a meaningful addition to Colorado's grid demand. The absence of a published figure, combined with the facility's absence from Google's own location list, suggests it does not register as part of Google's disclosed capacity footprint for purposes of understanding hyperscale infrastructure deployment.
